title: Runbook Weaver: convert runbooks into idempotent support micro-tasks and admin utilities
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a system (Runbook Weaver) that ingests canonical runbooks and outputs executable, idempotent micro-tasks and admin utilities. Goals: reduce mean time to remediation for common incidents, increase runbook replayability for oncall, surface safe quick-actions in the admin console, and enable telemetry-linked regressions for runs. The feature will include a task runner, a guarded CLI, a console surface for short-circuit actions, and audit/telemetry hooks for each step.
acceptance_criteria: Authoring flow: convert an existing markdown runbook into a Runbook Weaver bundle and validate in dry-run mode
Safety: every step must declare required RBAC and be reversible or guarded by approval unless marked read-only
Idempotency: steps must be safe to re-run; runner records checkpoints and can skip completed steps
Observability: each run produces traces and structured events feeding the ops dashboard
Rollout: canary to 2 internal teams, fallback to manual playbook if errors > 5%
CLI and Console: same primitives available in both surfaces with consistent audit logs
decisions: Use a lightweight sidecar process for interactive admin step execution instead of heavy VMs to reduce operational overhead
Represent steps as typed actions with explicit preconditions and compensating steps to enforce idempotency
Store run state and checkpoints in existing ops-events bounded table to reuse telemetry and SLO tooling
Initial language: YAML + declarative step types; evaluate DSL in follow-up if authorship pain points emerge
tradeoffs: Sidecar vs serverless: sidecar gives faster interactive latency and local context but increases deployment complexity for Dedicated/Private customers
Declarative YAML: simple to onboard non-devs but less expressive than a full DSL — chosen to accelerate ship and enable safe runs
Strict RBAC on-step: reduces accidental remediation but increases friction for urgent oncall paths; will add temporary-elevation workflows in a later cycle

Measure MTTR improvement for the ten pilot runbooks and iterate on step primitives
